title: Design System: Alexandre Boucaud — Personal Site

display.purpose: The person's name in the hero, and nothing else. Display family is provisional — under review.

headline.purpose: Section titles; the contact tagline one step larger at clamp(1.6rem, 3.5vw, 2.1rem) / 1.25.

nav.purpose: Navigation links only — the one place the serif appears at small size.

body.purpose: The hero bio. The only text with a hard 420px measure.

body-small.purpose: Project descriptions, talk titles, sidebar values. Runs 0.78125rem–0.8125rem.

label.purpose: Every metadata label. Always uppercase, 500 weight, 0.5rem–0.625rem, tracked 0.14em–0.22em.

shadows.name: page-lift
shadows.purpose: The 960px sheet against its dark ground. The only shadow in the system — never reuse this value elsewhere.

motion.name: link-fade
motion.purpose: Global link hover — drops to 0.7 opacity.

motion.name: color-shift
motion.purpose: Nav links and body links shifting to Observatory Sage on hover.

motion.name: surface-shift
motion.purpose: Contact rows lifting from Paper to Card on hover.

motion.name: control-shift
motion.purpose: Carousel arrows and dots responding to hover.

motion.name: slide-crossfade
motion.purpose: The carousel cross-fade — the only slow motion in the system.

motion.name: autoplay-interval
motion.purpose: Carousel auto-advance cadence; paused on pointer enter, restarted on leave.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: The structural breakpoint: hero, projects, talks, contact and nav all reflow.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Tightens the nav for the smallest phones.

breakpoints.name: short-landscape
breakpoints.purpose: Cuts vertical padding and the photo band so short viewports show content, not margin.

breakpoints.name: no-hover
breakpoints.purpose: Supplies :active feedback where hover can never fire.

layout.name: sheet-max
layout.purpose: Hard cap on the page sheet. Nothing breaks out of it.

layout.name: hero-grid
layout.purpose: Bio panel / metadata sidebar; collapses to one column below 700px.

layout.name: projects-grid
layout.purpose: The gap is the divider; cards carry no border of their own.

layout.name: talk-grid
layout.purpose: Year / title / venue, baseline-aligned. Becomes 48px 1fr below 700px with the venue hidden.

layout.name: bio-measure
layout.purpose: The only hard measure in the system.

narrative.overview:
This is the homepage of someone who builds things that have to work. Everything on the page is a fact — an institution, a date, an experiment, a student, a photograph taken on a mountain — and the design's whole job is to present those facts at maximum density without ever raising its voice. Credibility comes from precision: hairline rules that actually align, a single accent used sparingly enough that it still means something, metadata set small and confidently rather than padded out to look important. Nothing here persuades. It states, accurately, and gets out of the way.

The structure is a bounded cream sheet, never wider than 960px, sitting on a dark ground. Inside it, two paper tones alternate to separate sections, and every division is drawn with a 0.5px line rather than a shadow or a gap. Density is deliberately high — the hero sidebar packs six labelled blocks into a column narrower than the bio beside it — but line-height stays generous (1.7–1.85) so the page reads calm rather than cramped. Thirteen first-hand photographs from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory sit in a full-width band at the page's midpoint; they are the one place the system stops being quiet.

One direction is deliberately unsettled. The display face is currently DM Serif Display, which pulls the page toward academic paper rather than engineer's homepage. That serif is recorded as the current implementation, not as a settled decision — it is the one token a future pass is expected to revisit. Everything else in this file is the standard.
keyCharacteristics: A bounded 960px sheet on a dark ground — never full-bleed
Two paper tones (#f4f2ee recessed, #ffffff raised) doing all the sectioning
0.5px hairline rules as the only structural device
Completely flat: one shadow exists in the entire system
One accent, used only on links, tags, and live actions
Tiny wide-tracked uppercase labels as the connective tissue
Square corners by default; radius is the exception, never the rule
Real photography given a full-width band and honest credits

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Observatory Sage is the system's only chromatic color, and it appears only on things that are links, tags, or live actions. It never fills a surface, never backs a block of text, and never gets a companion accent. Its scarcity is what makes it legible.

rules.name: The Two Paper Rule
rules.body: Only two surfaces exist: Paper (recessed) and Card (raised). Sections separate by alternating between them — never by tinting, never by adding a third tone. If a new surface seems necessary, the layout is wrong.

rules.name: The Micro-Label Rule
rules.body: Metadata labels are always Space Grotesk 500, at or below 0.625rem, uppercase, tracked at 0.14em or wider, in Subtle Ink or the accent. The wide tracking is what makes type this small legible — never set a label at small size without it. The tracking scale is deliberate: 0.22em for the tightest-set keys, 0.2em for tags and subheads, 0.14em for section meta and photo captions.

rules.name: The Serif Is For Names Rule
rules.body: The display face appears only on proper titles: the person's name, section titles, the contact tagline, and nav links. It never sets body copy, never sets a label, and never appears below 1.15rem.

rules.name: The Sub-Rem Rule
rules.body: Almost nothing on this page is set at or above 1rem. Body copy runs at 0.9675rem and supporting text at 0.6875rem–0.8125rem. The smallness is the aesthetic — it reads as technical documentation rather than marketing. Preserve it; do not fix the page by scaling type up.

rules.name: The Bounded Sheet Rule
rules.body: Content is capped at 960px and the page is always a finite object on a ground, never an edge-to-edge website. Any new section lives inside the sheet.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every structural division in the system is a 0.5px line in Hairline — section borders, card seams, sidebar dividers, table rows. Not 1px, not a shadow, not a color change alone.

rules.name: The Flat-Except-the-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow except the page sheet itself — not at rest, not on hover, not on focus. If an element needs to separate from its neighbor, give it a 0.5px hairline or move it to the other paper tone.

rules.name: The Square-By-Default Rule
rules.body: New surfaces get 0 radius. A radius above 4px does not exist in this system, and rounding a card or a section would break the seam grid that the project layout depends on.

rules.name: The No Lost Content Rule
rules.body: Nothing is removed from a narrow screen because it does not fit. Content that cannot sit side by side stacks, wraps, or moves below its heading — display: none is for a control that has been replaced by a better one at that size, never for a fact the visitor came to read.

dos: Do keep every new surface inside the 960px sheet and give it square corners.
Do separate things with a 0.5px Hairline rule or by switching between the two paper tones.
Do set every metadata label in Space Grotesk 500, uppercase, 0.625rem or smaller, tracked at 0.14em or wider.
Do reserve Observatory Sage for links, category tags, and live actions — and keep it rare enough to still read as a signal.
Do use the display face for names and section titles only.
Do give real photographs their captions and credits verbatim, always over the bottom scrim.
Do keep transitions short and colorless — 0.15s for links and hovers, 0.2s for control backgrounds. The only slow motion in the system is the carousel's 1s cross-fade.
Do match any new dot to a new slide, one for one.
donts: Don't add a shadow to anything. One shadow exists and it belongs to the page sheet.
Don't introduce a second accent color or a semantic color set.
Don't fill a surface with Observatory Sage or set text on top of it.
Don't round a card, section, or panel beyond the established 3px / 4px exceptions.
Don't scale the type up to make the page feel friendlier — the sub-1rem scale is the aesthetic.
Don't use a 1px border where the system uses 0.5px.
Don't set body copy or labels in the display face.
Don't treat the photographs as decoration that can be cropped, swapped for stock, or stripped of credits.
Don't hide content on small screens to make a layout fit. Stack it, wrap it, or move it under its heading instead.
